scope: Statewide
summary: Would stop Virginia localities from granting final rezoning, special-use or site-plan approval for any new data center, of any size, until pending data center grid interconnection requests are met or July 1, 2028.
status_detail: Carried over to 2027 · Continued in House Rules by voice vote, 2/6/26

scope: Local option (state bill lets municipalities pause)
summary: Lets any municipality pause new data center applications for up to 180 days, retroactive to the meeting notice, so a developer could face a local freeze site by site; reuse is barred for 18 months.
status_detail: Pending – passed one chamber · House passed 201-1 on 2026-06-24; Senate Local Government reported as amended 2026-06-30 (Senate amended Printer's No. 3727), re-referred to Senate Rules 2026-06-30. Would need House concurrence.

scope: Local option (state bill lets municipalities pause)
summary: Lets a municipality bar filing or review of applications for data centers of 25 MW or more IT load for up to 18 months, with a hardship waiver; a local option.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to House Local Government 2026-05-27; no further action.

scope: Local option (state bill lets municipalities pause)
summary: Lets a municipality, by resolution, stop accepting applications for data centers of 25 MW or more IT load for up to 18 months, retroactive to notice; projects tied to existing power plants are exempt.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-04; reported as committed and re-referred to Rules 2026-06-30; re-reported as amended 2026-07-11; second consideration 2026-07-12; re-referred to Rules 2026-09-30. No floor vote.

scope: Statewide
summary: Would stop any new or expanded data center of 20 MW or more (1 MW in small utility areas), and the power supply built for it, from state or local permits for 36 months.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Referred to Senate Local Government 2026-06-04; no further action.
threshold: 20 MW+ (1 MW+ in utilities under 2,500 MW peak)

scope: Statewide
summary: Would impose a six-month statewide freeze from enactment on any approval, permit, subsidy or tax incentive for building or expanding AI data centers over 10 MW, while a commission studies impacts.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-09-14; referred to Assembly State and Local Government Committee

scope: Statewide
summary: Would halt construction of new data centers of 25 MW or more IT load and all state or local siting and operating permits until 90 days after a DEP study, roughly 18 months at most.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-10-19; referred to Assembly Science, Innovation and Technology Committee

scope: Statewide

status_detail: In effect; no fixed end date

scope: Statewide
summary: A statewide pause: no county, municipality or agency could approve or permit construction of a new 100 MW+ data center through January 31, 2027, while the legislature runs studies.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-06-30 and assigned to Senate Executive Committee; motion to suspend rules failed 6-15 (2026-06-30; one vote list dates it 2026-07-27).

scope: Statewide
summary: Would freeze all Michigan data center approvals until April 1, 2027: no local permits, no state permits, and no new operation, with fines up to $1,000 a day, at any size.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-02-26; referred to Government Operations; no further action

scope: Statewide
summary: Would stop the Michigan Public Service Commission from approving any utility contract, tariff, discount or rate for a data center until April 1, 2027, blocking new power service deals in the interim.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-02-26; referred to Government Operations; no further action

scope: Statewide

status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-02-26; referred to Government Operations; no further action

scope: Statewide
summary: Until April 1, 2027, localities and the state environment department could not issue any approval for any data center, and no one could begin operating one, with $1,000 per day fines for operating.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-06-04; referred to Government Operations; no further action through 2026-09-30.

scope: Statewide
summary: Until April 1, 2027, the PSC could not approve any contract, tariff, discount or rate between an electric utility and a data center, which would stall new utility service deals for data centers in that period.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Introduced 2026-06-04; referred to Government Operations; no further action through 2026-09-30.

scope: Statewide
summary: Bars any state or local permit for siting, building or operating a 20 MW+ data center until 90 days after DEC rules (no sooner than 3 years) and PSC rate actions. Existing permits can be renewed or modified.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Amended 10141a and recommitted to Environmental Conservation 2026-05-12; no vote.

scope: Statewide
summary: A one-year state permit moratorium for 20 MW+ data centers, then a 3-month-ahead public hearing, separate rate classes (1 MW+ definition), 90% renewable use by 2040 for 5 MW+ sites, host-community funding and prevailing wage.
status_detail: Pending – passed both chambers · Senate passed 43-17 and Assembly passed 103-38 on 2026-06-04 (Senate substituted for S10642); no governor action shown by 2026-09-30.
threshold: 20 MW+ (moratorium, rate class); 5 MW+ (renewable standards, labor); 1 MW+ (base definition)

scope: Statewide
summary: Bars all state and local siting permits and approvals for 100 MW+ datacenters from 2026-08-01 to 2028-08-01. Also funds an impact study and adds annual documentation to keep sales tax exemptions.
status_detail: Pending – in committee · Filed 2026-04-30; first reading and referred to House Rules 2026-05-05. No floor vote.
